title: Bootstrap stream coordinator and KV temperature prober
creator: Anika Bose
description:
Problem statement: Dedicated fleets still observe tail latency spikes and transient SLA misses during tenant on-ramps and bursty traffic due to expensive shard pulls and cold KV caches. Existing approaches either blanket-prefetch too much (wasting network and memory) or rely on blunt LRU seeding that misses short-lived hot prefixes. This ticket proposes a coordinated two-component system: (1) a Bootstrap Stream Coordinator (BSC) that orchestrates staged, bandwidth-aware weight streaming and shard handoffs, and (2) a KV Temperature Prober (KTP) that scores and selects KV prefixes for targeted priming. Together they reduce cold-start cost, respect throughput guarantees, and play nicely with autoscaling policies.

Design goals and constraints: ensure warmup latency reduction without oversubscribing network or interfering with steady-state inference; support multi-tenant fairness and priority policies (reserved capacity vs burst tiers); provide knobs for graceful degradation when the fleet is saturated; integrate with Dedicated autoscaler to avoid thrash; emit metrics for chargeback and SLO verification.

Key mechanisms:
- Bootstrap Stream Coordinator (BSC): a centralized per-fleet controller that accepts warmup plans from admission control. BSC slices a tenant's weight transfer into time-bounded tranches using a bandwidth budget calculated from fleet capacity and current traffic. Tranches are scheduled with soft priorities (tenant SLAs, active sessions, expected QPS). BSC supports three streaming modes: eager (high-priority full prefetch), progressive fidelity (download smaller low-precision quantized slices first), and background-throttle (best-effort prefetch when idle). BSC exposes an HTTP API for plan proposals, with responses that include an SLA-safe schedule and estimated completion ETA.
- KV Temperature Prober (KTP): distributed lightweight agent that computes a temperature score per KV prefix based on recency, frequency, tenant session affinity, and a model-derived importance heuristic (a compact stateless estimator that predicts expected token reuse). KTP maintains a small approximate set (Bloom filter / Count-min sketch) for memory-efficient signals and periodically elects top-k prefixes for priming. The scoring formula is tunable (weights for recency/frequency/affinity) and can be warmed from recent traces.
- Admission & backpressure: BSC enforces a global bandwidth threshold and emits backpressure signals to the autoscaler and to tenant admission. When bandwidth budget is low, BSC downgrades streaming mode (e.g., from eager to progressive fidelity) and may postpone non-critical tenants. The autoscaler can use BSC signals to provision transient capacity or shift tenants to burst pools.
- Progressive fidelity format: integrate with existing weight snapshot format to support slice-level precision hints. Small first slices allow model tokens to serve at near-cold cost but with faster availability; higher-quality slices stream in the background.
- Network-aware tranche sizing: tranche sizes computed from observed egress rates and measured shard fetch latency to avoid saturating the interconnect. Tranche size decays with concurrent streaming jobs to maintain inference throughput.

Metrics and SLOs to track:
- Median and P95 cold-start latency (time from first request to stable P90 latency)
- Volume of prefetched bytes per tenant and per successful request (efficiency)
- KV priming hit rate and prefix selection precision (TPR/FPR)
- Number of scheduled tranches downgraded due to backpressure
- Correlation of warmup activity with autoscaler scale-ups

Implementation plan (phased):
1) Spec + API (2w): finalize BSC datamodel, tranche lifecycle, KTP scoring formula, and admission signals. Add schema for progressive-fidelity slices. Document in Confluence and design review.
2) KTP PoC (3w): implement lightweight agent in serving node that produces temperature scores and a proto for top-k exports. Validate on replayed traces in staging.
3) BSC PoC (3w parallel): implement a controller as a Kubernetes deployment in dedicated control plane; support plan proposals and simple throttling logic. Wire plan proposals from the Console UI as a toggle.
4) Integration + e2e test (2w): hook KTP outputs to BSC, run traffic replays, measure cold-start latencies and network usage across small fleet, iterate.
5) Canary rollout (4w): enable for low-impact tenants, monitor SLOs, and adjust scoring weights and tranche sizing heuristics.

Rollout and feature flags: feature-flag BSC scheduling per-fleet and allow tenants to opt into eager mode. Expose config in the Console: bandwidth budget, priority tiers, progressive-fidelity toggle.

Observability and dashboards: new Grafana panels for warmup bandwidth, per-tenant prefetched bytes, KV temperature distribution heatmaps, and a tracer span for bootstrap sessions. Create an alert when prefetched bytes / successful requests ratio exceeds threshold (indicating wasted prefetch).

Testing strategy: unit tests for tranche lifecycle, integration tests for streaming under synthetic bandwidth constraints, chaos tests that kill streaming jobs mid-way to ensure graceful rollback and KV state consistency, and load tests in staging with scaled playback of production traces.

Security and compliance: no customer data movement outside existing encrypted channels; BSC and KTP operate on metadata and model weights only. Add an audit log entry for every scheduled tranche (release-level requirement for Private deployments). Marked for security review if progressive-fidelity requires new snapshot encryption semantics.

Risks and mitigations: risk of over-prefetch causing network contention -> mitigate via conservative default budgets and automatic downgrade heuristics; inaccurate KTP predictions -> mitigate with fallbacks to frequency-based seeding and continuous retraining of the lightweight estimator; cross-tenant fairness concerns -> BSC enforces quota and priority policy and exposes tenant-level metrics for ops.

Compatibility and dependencies: integrates with existing weight snapshot format and runtime slice loader; depends on autoscaler signals (ENG-110234) and on shard-hand-off work (ENG-30512). Backwards compatible with fleets that do not opt in (BSC remains idle).
comments: 2026-02-26 - Anika Bose: Initial draft posted. Shared in #dedicated-infra channel. Asked SRE for bandwidth telemetry availability.
2026-03-02 - Priya Singh (SRE): Confirmed per-node egress metrics exist; suggested adding a per-tenant cap at the BSC level to avoid noisy tenants monopolizing links.
2026-03-04 - Marco Alvarez: Implementing KTP PoC. Chose Count-min sketch + small bloom filter for prefix candidates. Initial microbenchmark shows <200us overhead per scoring pass.
2026-03-06 - Lila Hart (Design): Reviewed Console UX for opt-in toggle and bandwidth slider; recommended clearer language around 'progressive fidelity' to avoid customer confusion.

2026-03-08 - Ethan Cho (Runtime): Ran a replay in staging with progressive-fidelity slices (8-bit delta first). Cold-start P95 improved ~28% but total prefetched bytes increased ~12%—need to tune tranche sizes.

2026-03-10 - Marco Alvarez: BSC tranche scheduler prototype merged to feature branch. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-runtime/pull/1829. Next: integrate with autoscaler signals and add canary gates.
